newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Spanish group to invest $150 mln in Rio gas firms.
newsitem.headline: Spanish group to invest $150 mln in Rio gas firms.

text.p: The winning consortium of today's auction of Rio de Janeiro state gas firms Companhia Estadual de Gas (CEG) and Riogas said it plans to invest more than $150 million over the next five to six years.
Antoni Llarden, corporate director of Industrial Development at Spain's Gas Natural SDG SA, said he believes there will be a large development in the Brazilian natural gas sector.
"We want to develop a natural gas network that can satisfy levels of gas demand projected for the year 2,000," he told a news conference.

Gas Natural SDG SA, along with Spain's Iberdrola Investimentos Sociedade Unipessoal LDA, U.S. firm Enron and Argentine Pluspetrol Energy SA, bought a controlling stake in CEG and Riogas for 622.2 million reais.
Spanish group Repsol owns 45 percent of Gas Natural SDG SA and Pluspetrol Energy SA.
Llarden said he expects the number of clients to increase by 600,000 in eight to 10 years.
He also also said the group has no plans to raise prices and cut jobs.
The president of CEG, Hequel Ozorio, said the priority of this privatization was to convert the CEG network into a natural gas network and expand gas for commercial, residential and industrial use.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
